<explanation>
1. Identify the project type and purpose
   - SurfSense is a full-stack research assistant platform. It consists of:
     • A Python-based backend (FastAPI, database, ingestion & RAG pipelines, connectors, background tasks)  
     • A Next.js/React TypeScript frontend (dashboard, search/chat UI)  
     • A browser extension (Plasmo, TS) to capture web content  
   - Purpose: Let users ingest personal docs and external sources, perform hybrid search + RAG, chat with cited answers.

2. Analyze the file structure
   - Top level:
     • `surfsense_backend/` – FastAPI app, Alembic migrations, Dockerfile, tasks, connectors, agents  
     • `surfsense_web/` – Next.js app with App Router, API routes under `/app/api`, UI components, hooks, lib, content/docs  
     • `surfsense_browser_extension/` – Plasmo extension, background scripts, popup React UI, utils  
     • `docker-compose.yml`, `DOCKER_SETUP.md` – orchestrates backend + database  
   - Patterns:
     • Backend layered by routers (routes/), schemas/, utils/, tasks/  
     • RAG pipeline using LangGraph/LangChain, hybrid search modules (retriver/)  
     • Frontend uses React components, server/client components under Next.js app folder  
     • Extension is a thin client sending data to backend API

3. Examine the README for technical insights
   - Backend tech: FastAPI, PostgreSQL + pgvector, SQLAlchemy, Alembic, LangGraph, LangChain, LiteLLM/Ollama, advanced hybrid search, background tasks  
   - Frontend tech: Next.js, React, TS, Vercel AI SDK Stream Protocol, Tailwind, Shadcn, Zod, React Hook Form  
   - Extension tech: Plasmo (Manifest v3)

4. Main components & their interactions
   a. SurfSense Backend (Docker container)
      - FastAPI service exposing REST/WebSocket endpoints  
      - Database (PostgreSQL + pgvector) for users, docs, embeddings, connectors, chats  
      - Background tasks module for connector indexing, streaming connector search  
      - RAG pipeline:  
         • Ingestion → Chonkie chunking → Embedding via AutoEmbeddings → Store in PGVector  
         • Hybrid retriever combining vector + full-text search → Reranker service   
         • Chat agents (LangGraph nodes/graphs) orchestrating prompts + LLM calls  
      - External connectors: GitHub, Linear, Notion, Slack, Tavily, LinkUp, YouTube  

   b. SurfSense Web Frontend (Next.js)
      - User authentication (Google OAuth, JWT) via FastAPI Users  
      - Dashboard, search spaces, connectors management  
      - Chat UI using Vercel AI SDK Stream Protocol  
      - Calls backend API routes (`/app/api/search`, `/surfsense_backend/app/routes/*`)  

   c. SurfSense Browser Extension
      - Background script captures page data/auth  
      - Popup UI for API key, saving pages (sends to backend ingestion endpoint)  
      - Uses common utils and interfaces to serialize data  

   d. External / Supporting services
      - OAuth provider (Google)  
      - Local LLMs via Ollama (connected over HTTP/UNIX socket)  
      - Embedding / Reranker APIs (external if not local)  

5. Architectural patterns & design principles
   - Layered architecture in backend: API → Service/Utils → Database → Background tasks  
   - RAG as a Service: decoupling ingestion, retrieval, ranking, and generation  
   - Micro-frontend flavor in Next.js: separate route modules, hooks, UI components  
   - Extension as thin client: leverages same backend API  

6. Drawing your system design diagram
   - Step A: Draw 4 horizontal tiers (or columns), color-code each tier:
     1. Clients (Browser, Mobile, Extension) – light blue  
     2. Frontend (Next.js) – teal  
     3. Backend (FastAPI) – green  
     4. Data & Services – orange  

   - Step B: Place components:
     • Clients:  
        – Web browser (renders Next.js)  
        – Browser Extension  
     • Frontend:  
        – Next.js Server Components & API Routes  
        – React Chat UI (Vercel AI SDK)  
     • Backend:  
        – FastAPI App  
          · Routers (chats, documents, connectors, search)  
          · Agents module (LangGraph nodes/graphs)  
          · Tasks worker  
          · Connectors modules  
          · Utils (embedding, reranker, streaming)  
     • Data & Services:  
        – PostgreSQL + pgvector  
        – Alembic (migration tooling)  
        – Local/Remote LLM (Ollama/LiteLLM)  
        – External APIs (GitHub, Slack, Notion, Linear, Tavily, LinkUp, YouTube)  

   - Step C: Draw arrows to show data flow:
     • User → Next.js UI → REST calls → FastAPI → DB  
     • FastAPI → background tasks → external connectors → DB  
     • FastAPI → RAG pipeline → LLM → Response → Frontend → User  
     • Extension → FastAPI ingestion endpoint  
     • Next.js → calls backend search API → hybrid search → returns embeddings  

   - Step D: Annotate with technologies:
     • On each box, list key frameworks (e.g., “FastAPI + SQLAlchemy”, “Next.js + React + TS”, “Ollama/LiteLLM”)  
     • Indicate ports (e.g., 8000 for FastAPI, 3000 for Next.js) if relevant  

7. Tailoring diagram for a full-stack application
   - Emphasize clear frontend vs backend separation  
   - Highlight the API layer between Next.js and FastAPI  
   - Show DB interactions and background pipelines distinctly  
   - Include external systems (OAuth, connectors, LLM hosts) as separate boxes  

8. Diagramming guidelines
   - Use consistent shapes:  
     • Rectangles for services/components  
     • Cylinders for databases  
     • Clouds for external services/APIs  
   - Color-code by layer (client, presentation, application, data)  
   - Label each connection with protocol/format (HTTP, REST, WebSocket, gRPC)  
   - Use directional arrows to indicate request/response or data flow  
   - Number major flows (1,2,3…) to guide readers through the sequence  

9. Final tips
   - Be exhaustive: break down large modules (e.g., agents vs connectors vs tasks)  
   - Don’t clutter: group related subcomponents under a single box if too detailed  
   - Keep it readable: use spacing, legends, and consistent styling  
   - Update diagram as project evolves (new connectors, services, or migration paths)  
   - Review with devs to ensure accuracy

By following these steps and focusing on the separation of concerns, data flows, and technology stacks, you will produce a detailed, accurate system design diagram perfectly tailored to SurfSense’s architecture. Make sure to capture every major component, its dependencies, and interactions to give stakeholders and new engineers a clear end-to-end view of the system.  
</explanation>
